title: G3O codebook v2.7 review
background:
T-010 (G3O reclassification, Output Contract v2.7 / validate v1.5). Per your ruling S1 the codebook becomes the single source of truth, linked by code to the jev question sets and the extractor prompts, and shared by the procurement and AI-text-detection pipelines. Three fresh-context subagents (Claude Code, claude-opus-5-5) reviewed it adversarially, each item against the v2.5 contract on `main` (`375f1ff`), v2.6 (`052fcb2`, unpushed), the re-pilot 2 wording, CX-01.2 and SPEC v001.5. Every option other than `keep` was drafted by an agent; none carries a recommendation.

Your choices seed the contract slots, and you still write or line-edit every coding rule before the hash (A-001). Changing a CX-01.2 item needs re-signature (R-025), and any enum change costs two version steps (C-007).

The page verdict column holds v2.5 (4 values), and would have held v2.6 (4 values with changed meaning) and v2.7 (8 values) answers, with `confirms_absence` meaning something different in each. Comparability rests on the per-row contract version (R-050), which does not exist yet. A written crosswalk table (v2.5 <-> v2.7, both directions, with the non-mappable cells marked) is not in any document. (`C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/output_contract.md:224; 052fcb2:g3o/extract/prompts/output_contract.md:224; C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:71, 99`)

items.title: How the single source of truth is built (decide first: the other items are coded into it)
items.situation: Ruling S1 makes the codebook the source of truth, linked by code to the jev prompts and the extractor, across pipelines. This item picks the form.

options.label: One machine-readable codebook with generated artifacts
options.mechanism: A single file (YAML/JSON) in one repo: each item has an ID, version, grain, value list with definitions, missingness, coder type (jev Choice / extractor / deterministic / detector / human), and per-pipeline coverage tags. Generators emit jev question sets, extractor prompt sections, Python Literal enums/JSON Schemas, and the public data dictionary. Pipelines consume a released, versioned build (package or pinned commit) and CI fails if generated files differ from the build.
options.benefits: Programmatic linkage the 2026-10-29 ruling asks for; enum drift (X01, X03, X21) becomes impossible by construction; coverage matrix is a query, not a document; one diff shows any wording change for sign-off
options.risks: Up-front build before v2.7 deploys competes with the locked reclass plan; generated prompt prose may read worse than hand-edited text and CX-01.2/v2.7 wording is signed as text; one file across three repos needs a release process; a generator bug propagates everywhere
options.commits_to: Semantic versioning per item and per release; PI signs every item-wording change, integrator signs releases; procurement migrates by replacing contract.py with the generated module at a chosen release (Q-001 answered by that choice) and dropping the snapshot test; text repo replaces its vendored g3o/common/contract.py with the package

options.label: Core codebook plus pipeline modules
options.mechanism: Main owns the core (contract columns, page verdict, CX items) as machine-readable spec; procurement and text-detection own namespaced modules (proc.*, text.*) that may reference but not redefine core IDs. A compatibility table records which module version works with which core version. Generation is optional per module.
options.benefits: Respects ES §1 (extension, never replacement) and PS §13.1 (separate contract importing shared vocabularies); each team keeps release cadence; adversarial point: avoids loading procurement-only or detector-specific items into the observatory core
options.risks: Overlaps across modules (governance terms vs CX content_*, genre vs disclosure_form) are not forced to resolve; compatibility matrix must be maintained; a core enum change still costs coordinated bumps (C-007)
options.commits_to: Core versioned by main integrator with PI sign-off; module owners (procurement integrator DEC-009, text pipeline owner) version modules and sign mapping (PSPEC R-042); procurement migrates from v2.0 copy to 'core vX + proc module v1' at a coordinated step under RSPEC R-085/D-008

options.label: Status quo copies with automated sync checks
options.mechanism: Each pipeline keeps its own copy; CI in each repo fetches the live core contract at a pinned commit and diffs enums and versions; drift fails the build; changes travel as integrator deltas (as RSPEC D-008 already plans).
options.benefits: Smallest change before v2.7 deployment; no new tooling repo; teams keep full control
options.risks: Copies still exist, so semantic drift (definitions, grain, rules like R-041) passes enum diffs; cross-repo CI needs read access to the private main repo; the PI ruling on a single source of truth is met only procedurally
options.commits_to: A named owner of the sync check per repo; procurement replaces its snapshot-only test (WT tests/test_core.py L121) with a live diff; delta protocol per C-007

options.label: Shared code package without full generation
options.mechanism: Extract g3o/common/contract.py (and jev question definitions) into a small installable package that all pipelines import at a pinned version; prose contract remains hand-written, with a test asserting prose tables match the package enums.
options.benefits: Fixes vendored-copy drift (X21) with less build than A1; matches PSPEC R-043 'shared dependency, not a copy'
options.risks: Prompts and docs remain hand-synced; definitions (not just enums) can still diverge; packaging a private repo for RA environments
options.commits_to: Package versioning tied to contract version; integrator releases; procurement imports package instead of contract.py

options.label: Federated instruments with a signed crosswalk
options.mechanism: Each pipeline keeps its own instrument; a crosswalk file maps each pipeline variable to a core item ID with a status (same/variant/new/internal) and transformation rule; consolidation applies the crosswalk at ingest.
options.benefits: Honest about different constructs (AI-text estimands are not adoption codes); no forced merger of signed wording

items.body:
**Current text (verbatim)**

v2.5 (production) §4.7:

- `confirms_activity` | Source documents a specific GenAI activity at this institution
- `confirms_absence` | The supplied page text contains no GenAI evidence relevant to this institution
- `ambiguous` | Source mentions AI but unclear whether generative AI, or mentions GenAI but unclear whether this institution is involved
- `background_only` | Source provides general context (country AI strategy, vendor overview) but does not document activity at this specific institution

SPEC R-015 (locked): "Page-verdict vocabulary has 8 values: the 7 re-pilot 2 values (`confirms_activity`, `ambiguous_genai`, `ambiguous_attribution`, `other_body` = v2.6 `other_actor`, `event_only` = v2.6 `excluded_event`, `background_only`, `no_genai`) plus v2.5 `confirms_absence` (page states absence; distinct from `no_genai`, no relevant content). It replaces v2.5 `genai_evidence` in the same column."

Re-pilot 2 jev instruction (unclear2.py L84-85): "Code this PAGE for the named institution only, using only what the page says. Does it document a generative-AI activity at this institution? If several values fit, take the first in this order." Definitions at unclear2.py L33-54 (confirms_activity text quoted under C02/C04; `event_only`: "The only GenAI content is a public-facing event, workshop, seminar, showcase or educational programme, with no documented adoption, procurement, deployment or governance by the institution itself (WS10 D1: not a qualifying activity)."; `background_only`: "The page gives only general context (national AI strategy, vendor overview, news about GenAI in general) and documents no activity at this institution."; `no_genai`: "The page contains no generative-AI content relevant to this institution.")

**Reviewer findings**

- **high** · semantic-drift / comparability: The token `confirms_absence` carries three different meanings in the same column: v2.5 = page has no GenAI evidence (the v2.7 `no_genai`); v2.6 = excluded event OR no qualifying content OR definite other actor; v2.7 R-015 = "page states absence". R-015 keeps v2.5 rows unconverted in the same column and relies on the row's contract version. Any query or join that pools rows by value without filtering on version will silently mix these meanings. (`C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/output_contract.md:224; 052fcb2:g3o/extract/prompts/system_prompt.md:72-74; C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:71`)
- **high** · undefined-category: v2.7 `confirms_absence` ("page states absence") has no operational definition, worked example, or position in the first-in-order list, and was never piloted (re-pilot 2 had 7 values; report-repilot2.json has no such value). Open cases: "the council does not currently use AI"; an AI register listing zero systems; a ban on GenAI use. The ban is qualifying governance under WS10 D2 (Central Coast fixture, expected `qualifying`), so the value overlaps `confirms_activity` unless the definition excludes rules. (`C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:71; H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/report-repilot2.json; 052fcb2:tests/fixtures/exval_cases.json case Central Coast`)
- **high** · empirical / attribution: `ambiguous_attribution` was chosen on 0 of 372 re-pilot 2 pages (highest probability on any page 0.31) while `other_body` was chosen on 59. Once `other_body` existed, the uncertain-attribution value effectively disappeared. Because `other_body` maps to v2.6 `other_actor` and then to source-bounded absence, uncertain attribution may now be recorded as definite other-body and count toward an institution `no`. The handoff reports attribution errors 12 -> 3 against the Pilot 4 agent read, but that read is not a gold set. (`H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/answers-repilot2.jsonl (0 of 372 pages); H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/report-repilot2.json; H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/HANDOFF.md:100-101`)
- **high** · reliability / confidence: In re-pilot 2, 284 of 372 page answers (76%) had confidence below 0.8: no_genai 110/149, event_only 41/50, other_body 44/59, ambiguous_genai 49/52, background_only 28/34, confirms_activity 12/28. Median confidence was 0.46-0.59 for every value except confirms_activity (0.83). Under R-081 each of these is downgraded. Caveat: the sample is 250 institutions that v2.5 coded unclear (hard cases), so it is not representative of the back-fill. This depends on the downgrade item owned by the other reviewer. (`H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/answers-repilot2.jsonl (computed: 284 of 372 page answers confidence < 0.8)`)
- **medium** · chunk-combination conflict: R-044 says "Page fields take the first chunk's value", but the re-pilot combined chunks by first-in-order, which is what produced the reported numbers. On the cited page, chunk 1 = ambiguous_genai (0.25) and chunk 2 = confirms_activity (0.31): the re-pilot rule gives confirms_activity and R-044 gives ambiguous_genai. The codebook has to say which rule governs the verdict. (`C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:R-044; H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/unclear2.py:137; H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/answers-repilot2.jsonl key r20261018T154238Z-c0e5|INST-0032750|60d0cd02f257862154339674d00f6c7c`)
- **medium** · non-exclusive categories / order dependence: The values are not mutually exclusive (one page can hold another body's activity, an event, and a stray generic-AI sentence). Classification therefore depends on the "take the first in this order" instruction. The order also makes substantive choices: `ambiguous_genai` ranks above `other_body` and `event_only`, so one generic "AI strategy" sentence turns a settled other-body or event page into unclear. jev's probability output does not show whether the order instruction was applied. (`H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/unclear2.py:85; H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/report-repilot2.json page_old_to_new`)
- **medium** · overlap: `background_only` ("news about GenAI in general") and `other_body` (a GenAI activity of a different body) overlap for news about another government's deployment. Between re-pilots, 14 pages moved background_only -> other_body. (`H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/unclear2.py:47-53; H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/report-repilot2.json (background_only -> other_body 14 pages)`)
- **medium** · missing state: v2.6 had an `inaccessible` disposition (failed access, mapped to ambiguous). The 8 values have nothing for failed fetches, empty text or raw `%PDF` bytes. The handoff notes 2 re-pilot confirms that rested on raw-PDF text (URL and title only). R-074 re-scrapes such pages, but pages that still fail need a verdict or a named pipeline state. (`052fcb2:g3o/common/evidence_review.py:61-63; H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/HANDOFF.md:106`)
- **low** · crosswalk: v2.7 -> v2.5 maps many-to-one except `background_only` and the new `confirms_absence`. v2.5 -> v2.7 is one-to-many (`ambiguous` splits in two; v2.5 `confirms_absence` splits into no_genai / event_only / other_body). The two directions are not symmetric, and no crosswalk table is written down. (`C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/output_contract.md:223-226; C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:71`)

**Notes**

The downgrade threshold (R-081), supporting text, and source_type/credibility are owned by the other reviewer; finding 4 is reported here only because it decides how the verdict works in practice.

items.situation: Existing item · linkage: `jev-choice` · source: `C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/system_prompt.md:11-23; 052fcb2:g3o/extract/prompts/system_prompt.md:58-59; H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/unclear2.py:36, 41-44; C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:72` · 6 finding(s), 2 high. items.body:
**Current text (verbatim)**

v2.5 system prompt L11: "**Include:** large language models (GPT, Claude, Gemini, LLaMA, Mistral, etc.), text-to-image generators, code-generation tools (GitHub Copilot, Amazon CodeWhisperer), sovereign/national LLMs (France's Albert, etc.), GenAI-powered chatbots, and any tool explicitly described as using generative AI, LLMs, or foundation models." L13: "**Exclude:** traditional machine learning (fraud detection classifiers, predictive analytics), robotic process automation (RPA) without a generative component, rule-based chatbots without LLM backends, general "AI strategies" that do not specifically reference generative AI." L15-21: positive signal required (1 named LLM/product, 2 explicit generative-capability description incl. "drafts, writes, summarizes, translates, or generates", 3 explicit label); "A "chatbot," "virtual assistant," or "automation" mentioned **without** one of these three signals is not sufficient evidence of GenAI activity".

Re-pilot 2 (unclear2.py L36, L41-44): "The text must be explicitly generative AI (LLMs, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, AI chatbots, AI-generated content or equivalents) ... Generic 'AI', 'artificial intelligence', 'smart' systems, automation, analytics, prediction, transcription, translation, image or video recognition, or traditional machine-learning tools do not count unless the page says the tool generates text, images, audio, code or other content, or names a generative product or model (e.g. ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Claude, an LLM, an AI chatbot or AI assistant)."

SPEC R-016: "A named "AI chatbot" or "AI assistant" counts as generative and overrides the rule-based-chatbot exclusion (contract L12) for that naming. Contract §4.1 is unchanged: a generic "AI strategy" or "AI tools" stays `unclear`".

**Reviewer findings**

- **high** · conflict with retained fixtures: DEC-018 b keeps the 30 v2.6 fixtures as tests. Two of them expect holds on exactly the wording R-016 now makes positive. Clark Wilma ("AI Assistant Wilma Clark") has expected disposition `unresolved`, rationale "no explicit LLM/generative mechanism found". Cumberland Ask CCNC ("launches AI chatbot") is held. Under R-016 both become `confirms_activity`. The PI has to sign relabelled expectations, or the tests will fail. (`052fcb2:tests/fixtures/exval_cases.json cases Clark Wilma (review_record 3213), Cumberland Ask CCNC; C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/Stage5-Rulings.md:39 (DEC-018 b)`)
- **high** · construct validity / temporal: The contract itself says rule-based chatbots without LLM backends are excluded (L13) and that "chatbot", "virtual assistant" and similar words are "routinely" used for non-generative systems (L15). R-016 accepts the label "AI chatbot" / "AI assistant" with no date or mechanism condition, so non-generative assistants labelled "AI" code as GenAI. The error pushes prevalence upward, and it cannot be separated afterwards unless the basis for the GenAI call is stored (see A01). (`C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/system_prompt.md:13, 15; C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:72`)
- **medium** · internal contradiction (translation): v2.5 counts a system that "translates" as an explicit generative-capability signal (L18). Re-pilot 2 lists "translation" among things that "do not count unless the page says the tool generates" content. `interaction_type` also has a `translation` value. Whether machine translation counts as generating content is undecided. (`C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/system_prompt.md:18; H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/unclear2.py:42; C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/output_contract.md:197`)
- **medium** · reliability (one-word boundary): Under the merged rule, "virtual assistant" and "digital assistant" are still not evidence (v2.5 L15), but "AI assistant" is. One word now separates positive from ambiguous, and the codebook does not give equivalents in other languages (a multilingual-pipeline matter). Two coders, or jev across languages, will split on near-synonyms. (`C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/system_prompt.md:15; C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:72`)
- **medium** · scope breadth: "AI-generated content" and "content generation" count as GenAI. The Liverpool Plains fixture accepts GenAI by "functional inference" from "AI-enabled systems for research, content generation". Central Coast qualifies from one sentence refusing "Works created using AI or other generative technologies". The boundary now admits mentions as well as tools. This is consistent with WS10, but it widens the construct. (`052fcb2:tests/fixtures/exval_cases.json case Liverpool Plains (C05); H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/unclear2.py:36`)
- **low** · pointer precision: R-016 cites "contract L12" for the rule-based-chatbot exclusion and `system_prompt.md` L15 for the chatbot rule. The exclusion is system_prompt.md L13 (L12 is blank), and the chatbot sentence is L21 (L15 is the positive-signal paragraph). Someone editing by pointer could change the wrong sentence. (`C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:72; C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/system_prompt.md:13, 15, 21`)

**Notes**

The 17 ambiguous->no moves were ruled instrument error (Q-003 a). Any v2.7 question generated from the codebook must keep the sentence "generic 'AI strategy' / 'AI tools' stays ambiguous_genai" explicit.

options.label: v2.5 three-signal rule, chatbot alone not sufficient
options.mechanism: Positive only with a named model or product, an explicit generative-capability description, or an explicit GenAI label. Bare "chatbot" / "AI assistant" -> ambiguous.
options.benefits: Conservative and matches the v2.6 fixtures. Lower false-positive risk from legacy assistants.
options.risks: Misses real LLM chatbots that pages describe only as "AI chatbot". Reverses R-016 (Q7 b, SF-008 a).
options.commits_to: A PI re-ruling on R-016. No enum change. Re-pilot wording edited to drop "an AI chatbot or AI assistant" (as HANDOFF caveat ii suggested).

options.label: R-016: re-pilot 2 wording; named "AI chatbot" / "AI assistant" counts
options.mechanism: The re-pilot 2 confirms_activity text governs; v2.5 L15/L21 and v2.6 L58 are amended to match.
options.benefits: Already ruled; piloted wording; catches LLM chatbots described only by label.
options.risks: Upward bias from non-generative "AI" assistants, which cannot be undone afterwards. Fixture conflicts (Clark Wilma, Ask CCNC). The translation contradiction stays.
options.commits_to: Relabelled fixtures signed by the PI. A-012 fixtures. Amended system-prompt text. No enum change.

options.label: Agent-drafted: R-016 boundary plus a stored mechanism basis
options.mechanism: Keep R-016, and record for every positive which signal established GenAI (A01: named product/model, explicit label, generative capability described, named AI chatbot/assistant only). Also settle translation: (a) "translation counts only when the page ties it to a named GenAI product or says it is generated by an LLM", or (b) "translation counts as generative capability". The PI picks a or b.
options.benefits: Keeps the ruled boundary while letting analysts drop R-016-only positives in a robustness check. Resolves the translation contradiction explicitly.
options.risks: One more jev question per positive page. The PI still has to choose a or b on translation.
options.commits_to: Adding A01 (a new field: schema, API and site columns). A small re-pilot of the A01 question.

options.label: Agent-drafted: R-016 with a date condition
options.mechanism: "An 'AI chatbot' or 'AI assistant' counts as generative only when the page, or the activity's stated launch, is dated 2023 or later. Earlier or undated: `ambiguous_genai` unless another signal is present." Applied deterministically after jev from the publication or launch year.
options.benefits: Targets the legacy-assistant error directly.
options.risks: The cutoff year is arbitrary. Many pages are undated (v2.6: footer copyright is not a publication date), so undated LLM chatbots go back to ambiguous. Depends on source_publication_date quality (other reviewer).
options.commits_to: A deterministic rule that depends on a date field outside this scope. The PI chooses the cutoff year. Fixtures for dated and undated cases.

items.body:
**Current text (verbatim)**

v2.5 §4.1: "`yes` | At least one source documents a specific GenAI tool, pilot, policy, or deployment at this institution. `no` | All supplied pages for this institution have been reviewed and contain no mention of GenAI, LLMs, ChatGPT, Copilot, or equivalents. `unclear` | Ambiguous signals that could indicate GenAI activity but cannot be confirmed."

v2.6 system prompt (Per-page verdict): "A single supplied page cannot establish completion of the institution's remaining evidence review. Emit has_genai_activity=yes when this page supports a qualifying activity at the searched institution; otherwise emit unclear, including a clearly excluded event or no-qualifying-content page. Stage 6 determines a reviewed-evidence no only after the pipeline supplies complete context and no unresolved signal."

SPEC R-005: "institution-level `no` only with complete supplied context and no unresolved signal. An institution whose reviewed pages are all negative at confidence ≥ 0.8 gets `no` directly; the complete-context rule blocks `no` only when an unresolved signal remains (a low-confidence negative downgraded under R-081 counts as one)."

**Reviewer findings**

- **high** · definition contradicts ruling: The v2.5 `no` requires pages that "contain no mention of GenAI". Under WS10 D3 and the 8 values, event-only and other-body pages mention GenAI and still count as negative. Either the `no` text changes or event-only institutions can never be `no`. Production code follows a third rule: `no` iff every source is `confirms_absence` (jev_validate.py:421-422). (`C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/output_contract.md:147; H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-09-05-combined-ws10-review/DECISIONS-followup.md:23`)
- **high** · undefined negative set: R-005 does not say which of the 8 values are "negative". Candidates: no_genai, confirms_absence, event_only, other_body (v2.6 maps the last two to absence). `background_only` is unclear in v2.6 validate §3.1 (L58), yet the v2.6 rulings mention "benign background alongside completed event exclusion" (L13). The `no` count depends directly on this set. (`C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:65; 052fcb2:g3o/validate/prompts/output_contract.md:57-58; 052fcb2:docs/extraction-validation-rulings.md:13`)
- **high** · construct validity of the label: D3: "do not assert institution-wide nonuse". The published label (`none` on the site) reads as nonuse, while the evidence behind it is often one page (median ambiguous pages per unclear institution = 1, p90 = 5). `no` partly measures search depth. Nothing in the codebook records how much was reviewed (see A07). (`H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-09-05-combined-ws10-review/DECISIONS-followup.md:23; H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/HANDOFF.md:57`)
- **medium** · weakened guard: R-005's second sentence (all pages negative at ≥0.8 -> `no` directly) can be read as bypassing v2.6's coverage guard (completion markers, a matching artifact set, the attrition ledger, no non-benign failures). It does not say whether a page that failed to scrape or extract counts as an unresolved signal. (`C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:65; 052fcb2:docs/extraction-validation-rulings.md:13, 25`)
- **medium** · stale example: v2.5 Edge case A has one page emitting institution `no`. v2.6 only adds a note that such examples are "source-bounded" and leaves the example in place. A codebook that generates prompts would carry the contradicting example forward. (`C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/output_contract.md:303-315; 052fcb2:g3o/extract/prompts/output_contract.md:406-409`)
- **medium** · construct: what yes means: `yes` is triggered equally by a deployed tool, an agenda item proposing a policy (D4), staff training, or one prohibition clause (D2). The headline "documented" mixes use with intention and regulation (see A06). (`052fcb2:g3o/extract/prompts/output_contract.md:409-411; C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:67-69`)
- **low** · redundancy: In the two-pass design the page row already carries the page verdict. A page-level has_genai_activity limited to yes/unclear adds nothing and can disagree with the verdict. (`C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:61; 052fcb2:g3o/extract/prompts/system_prompt.md:113-119`)

**Notes**

Source-level completeness and the downgrade rule are the other reviewer's. The negative-set question has to be settled whichever option is chosen.

items.body:
**Current text (verbatim)**

v2.5 system prompt L29: "Check that the page actually pertains to the named institution and not a similarly-named entity (different country, different level of government, parent ministry rather than this agency, etc.). If the page describes a different entity, code `genai_evidence = confirms_absence`". L32 (step 4): GenAI not tied to this institution -> `ambiguous`. L33 (step 5): country-wide program without naming the institution -> `ambiguous` + `institution_attribution`. L52: "Attribute activities to the specific institution in the batch, not to its parent ministry or country. If a national initiative exists but this institution's participation is unconfirmed, use `unclear` with flag `institution_attribution`."

Re-pilot 2 confirms_activity (L37-41): "The activity must be carried out or adopted by the named institution itself. Exclude activity by a parent, higher-level or neighbouring body (e.g. a district, county, regency, region, consortium or city department when the named institution is a village, ward or sub-unit), by a similarly named organisation or company, and pages by vendors that only use the place name." `other_body` (L47-51): "The page documents a generative-AI activity, but it clearly belongs to a different body, not the named institution ...". `ambiguous_attribution` (L46).

v2.6 L39-46: observed actor separate from query target; "External speakers, service providers, courts, similarly named counties and joint projects do not inherit that identity."

**Reviewer findings**

- **high** · internal contradiction (parent body): v2.5 codes a parent-body page two ways: absence (L29, "parent ministry rather than this agency") and unclear with `institution_attribution` (L52). Re-pilot 2 makes it definite other_body. These are three treatments of one situation, and comparing v2.5 and v2.7 on parent-body pages mixes absence and unclear. (`C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/system_prompt.md:29 vs C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/system_prompt.md:52; H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/unclear2.py:38-40`)
- **high** · direction gap (sub-units): The rules cover only one direction: an activity by a higher body does not count for a lower one. They do not say whether a department's or unit's activity counts for its parent institution, or whether a court counts for its county (Butler: a court order recorded against the county). The master holds institutions at several levels, so one activity can be credited to both or to neither, and that changes prevalence. (`H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/unclear2.py:38-40; 052fcb2:tests/fixtures/exval_cases.json cases Butler (3197), Van Buren (C11)`)
- **medium** · joint and shared activity: Joint initiatives (Van Buren + St. Joseph) support participation, not sole ownership. The 8 values have no shared-participation state, and the joint case is at risk of being coded `other_body` when the page is framed as the other partner's. (`052fcb2:tests/fixtures/exval_cases.json case NotebookLM joint participation (C13); 052fcb2:g3o/extract/prompts/system_prompt.md:45-46`)
- **medium** · flag misuse in a worked example: Edge case F (vendor-only claim) codes `confirms_activity` and adds `institution_attribution`, a flag that means the activity "may belong to a parent ministry, sibling agency, or country-wide program". The example uses the flag for evidence quality, not attribution. (`C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/output_contract.md:361-367; C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/output_contract.md:266`)
- **medium** · evidence loss: An other_body page documents a real activity of an identifiable body. v2.6 stored that body in review.actors. The v2.7 items do not say whether the observed actor is extracted, and without it these observations cannot later go to the owner (as D5 did by hand for 114 activities). See A05. (`052fcb2:g3o/common/evidence_review.py:40-55; C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:N-005; H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-09-05-combined-ws10-review/OWNER-REPRESENTATION.md:11`)
- **low** · name-only matching: jev's state holds the institution name, country and level, but no parent/child hierarchy. Attribution is judged from names (example: Bloomburg TX was credited with Bloomsburg PA's activity). (`H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/HANDOFF.md:106; H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/unclear2.py:96-98`)

**Notes**

The WS10 combined correction (R-077) applies D5 owner transfers. Under N-005 these rules only classify; they never transfer.

items.body:
**Current text (verbatim)**

v2.6 system prompt L27-37: "Record institution-specific GenAI adoption, procurement, deployment, governance, and explicitly GenAI institution-specific proposals. Public workshops, talks and educational events are excluded even when the institution hosts, funds or attends. An event source can independently document a qualifying action: evaluate that separate action, not the venue. Institution-directed staff GenAI training qualifies; training does not establish tool deployment. Formal institution-issued rules for internal personnel OR external users qualify, including prohibitions, submission rules, and approved-tool/privacy conditions. Record the issuing body's governance action separately from software use. A draft or agenda can support proposed activity without proving enactment. Proposed activity has no new commitment bar. Preserve proposed, announced, pilot, production and discontinued distinctions."

SPEC R-010..R-013 (WS10 D1-D4). D1 approved wording: "A public-facing GenAI event or educational program is not itself a qualifying activity. An event page can support a separate record when it explicitly documents the institution's own adoption, procurement, deployment, or governance. A demonstration alone does not establish deployment."

**Reviewer findings**

- **high** · construct validity (incidental governance): One eligibility sentence in an artwork call ("Works created using AI or other generative technologies will not be accepted") is expected to be qualifying governance, which makes the institution `yes`. Clauses like this are routine in submission, grant, recruitment and education pages. D2 approved counting them, but the codebook records no form of the rule, so a full GenAI policy and a one-line clause both count as the same `yes` (see A03). (`052fcb2:tests/fixtures/exval_cases.json case Central Coast (C08); H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-09-05-combined-ws10-review/DECISIONS-followup.md:7`)
- **high** · reliability ("formal" undefined): "Formal institution-issued rules" is not defined. The fixtures show the line is hard to place: the Van Buren department-endorsed tool list with privacy rules is held `unresolved`, while the Central Coast single clause is `qualifying`. Unresolved/governance is the most common fixture category (6 of 30). (`052fcb2:tests/fixtures/exval_cases.json: 6 of 30 cases expected unresolved/governance (Van Buren C11, C12, Adams, Butler, and others)`)
- **medium** · stale fixture vs rule (training): The DECYP fixture expects `unresolved` / staff_training ("The signed rule does not explicitly settle whether institution-directed staff training itself qualifies"), but v2.6 L31 and the later ruling say it qualifies. The fixture's expectation predates the ruling. Also undefined: "institution-directed" (staff sent to a vendor webinar? an optional lunch-and-learn?). (`052fcb2:tests/fixtures/exval_cases.json case DECYP staff training (C19); 052fcb2:g3o/extract/prompts/system_prompt.md:31`)
- **medium** · breadth of proposals: D4 keeps proposals as qualifying with no commitment threshold. The fixtures make a contract clause letting a consultant upload deliverables to AI software (Ferguson) a qualifying proposal, and also an agenda item (Allen). Neither proves use, but both make the institution `yes` (see A06). (`052fcb2:tests/fixtures/exval_cases.json cases Ferguson (C07), Allen (3188); H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-09-05-combined-ws10-review/DECISIONS.md:23`)
- **medium** · boundary case: public service vs education: "Public-facing GenAI services remain eligible", but `event_only` covers any "educational programme". A library service giving the public supervised ChatGPT access, or an AI-literacy service with a GenAI tool, fits both. (`H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-09-05-combined-ws10-review/CODEBOOK-signoff-candidate.md:11; H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/unclear2.py:52`)
- **low** · jev suitability: The event exception (an event page that also documents a separate action) relies on first-in-order with confirms_activity first. That works for the verdict, but pass 2 then has to segment the separate action from the event (C07). (`H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/agent-workspace/2026-10-27-unclear-screen/unclear2.py:33-36, 52, 85`)

**Current text (verbatim)**

v2.5 §4.3: "`proposed` | Exploratory or hedged intent with no concrete commitment: "considering," "exploring," "studying feasibility," early discussions, unfunded or undated ideas. The text must still be explicitly generative-AI and tied to this institution. No named tool tied to a timeline, no signed MoU or contract, no budget line, no adopted policy. | `announced` | Publicly stated intent to deploy with a concrete, documented commitment but no evidence of actual use. Includes: MoUs, budget allocations without deployment, strategy timelines. | `pilot` | Limited deployment: subset of users/departments/use cases; described as trial/pilot/PoC/experiment; time-bounded. | `production` | Fully operational: available to intended user base, no longer experimental, in routine operations. | `discontinued` | Previously deployed but explicitly ended, cancelled, or suspended. | `unknown` | Evidence confirms GenAI activity exists but stage is indeterminate." "Permanent pilot" rule: "If described as "pilot" but running >12 months AND serving the full intended user base, code `production`."

Owed: procurement subproject amendment to `proposed` (R-087), text NOT yet received; this review drafts alternatives that procurement must agree.

**Reviewer findings**

- **high** · owed amendment / missing procurement state: The vocabulary has no procurement state. v2.6 "payment is procurement, not production" leads the Clay fixtures to `unknown`. The v2.5 system prompt (L43) counts "a signed MoU or contract" as a commitment, which makes a signed contract `announced`. So a contract is `announced` and a payment is `unknown`, two codes for the same kind of evidence. R-087 puts the procurement amendment in v2.7, but its text has not arrived. Every option below needs the procurement integrator's agreement. (`C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:136; 052fcb2:tests/fixtures/exval_cases.json cases Clay Business/Plus/unspecified (saved_field_changes adoption_stage unknown); C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/system_prompt.md:43`)
- **high** · chunk-safety: R-044: "ordered vocabularies take the first value in table order found in any chunk". Table order is proposed < announced < pilot < production < discontinued, so on a chunked page the least advanced stage found anywhere wins (e.g. a background paragraph mentioning "exploring" beats "now in production"). This contradicts the temporal rule "Record the most current status" (system prompt L54). (`C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:R-044; C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/system_prompt.md:54`)
- **medium** · stage semantics for non-tool actions: A published policy is coded `production` (Edge E, Merthyr), a draft `proposed` (Allen). `pilot` has no meaning for a policy, and `discontinued` needs "previously deployed", so a rescinded policy or a cancelled proposal has no value. The codebook does not write down the mapping for governance or training. (`C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/output_contract.md:359; 052fcb2:tests/fixtures/exval_cases.json cases Merthyr (2751), Allen (3188)`)
- **medium** · as-of date: "Record the most current status" cannot be done from one page. The stage is as of the page's date, not the access date. Without a stored as-of date (A08), a 2023 "pilot" page and a 2026 "production" page look like a conflict to Stage 6 rather than a progression. (`C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/system_prompt.md:54`)
- **medium** · rule not answerable by jev: The permanent-pilot rule needs duration (>12 months) and coverage (full user base), which a single page rarely gives and jev cannot work out across pages. Applied per page it will rarely fire, and when it does it will be unreliable. (`C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/output_contract.md:176`)
- **low** · wording ambiguity: v2.6 "Proposed activity has no new commitment bar" can be read as removing the commitment bar for `announced`. The bar still applies there; only `proposed` has none. (`052fcb2:g3o/extract/prompts/system_prompt.md:36; C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/system_prompt.md:41-43`)

**Notes**

The procurement amendment text is owed and was not seen. These options are drafts to discuss with the procurement integrator, not proposed text for them.

items.title: disclosure_form (CX-10..CX-18)
items.situation: Existing item · linkage: `jev-choice` · source: `H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/archive/planning-drive-copy-superseded-2026-10-26/launch-analysis-pr/index-design/codebook-extension-proposal.md:28-41` · 6 finding(s), 1 high. **Frozen CX-01.2 wording: any change needs re-signature (R-025).** Depends on: X14, X15, X16, X21.
items.body:
**Current text (verbatim)**

Question to jev: *What kind of document is this page?* One value. If several fit, take the first in table order.

- `register_cross_institution`: The page is, or is one entry in, a structured list of AI or algorithmic systems kept by a government body, with several entries in a common format (inventory, register, catalogue, algorithmic transparency record in a standard template), **and the list covers more than one institution** (a national or sectoral register, a standard-template record series across agencies).
- `register_single_institution`: As CX-10, but the list covers **one institution only** (e.g. a city's own table of its AI tools).
- `mandated_report`: The page is a document produced to meet a reporting obligation, such as a statutory annual-report section or a compliance or transparency report under a named rule.
- CX-13: The obligation may be named on the page **or inferred from the document's genre** (e.g. an annual report, a statutory compliance report). This is the one stated exception to CX-03.
- `formal_record`: An official one-off document of record from a government body: adopted policy or guidance, legislation, council or board minutes or resolutions, budget documents, procurement notice or award, audit or inspection report, **response to a freedom-of-information request**.
- `informal_official`: A government body's own communication with no reporting obligation and no standard format: press release, news item, blog, social post, speech, event page, service or FAQ page.
- `third_party`: Not published by a government body: news, vendor, academic, NGO or policy organization. A register entry quoted in a news article is `third_party` (code the page, not what it quotes).
- `unknown`: The page's kind cannot be determined from its text (e.g. an archived fragment with no header).

**Reviewer findings**

- **high** · construct validity: `mandated_report` is the top of the 'systematic' pole, but CX-12/13 do not require the obligation to concern AI or algorithmic disclosure. Any statutory annual report (most ministries, councils and agencies publish one by law) that mentions a chatbot in passing would code `mandated_report`, placing an incidental mention above a city's own AI register. CX-13 lets jev infer the obligation from genre, which is world knowledge (an exception to CX-03) and varies by country. Pilot counts are too small to test this: 3 of 285 (PILOT-REPORT.md:21) and 2 in pilot 2 (report-v2.json distribution). (`codebook-extension-proposal.md:35-36 (CX-12, CX-13); pilot/pilot.py:132 (question text: 'The obligation may be named on the page or inferred from the document's genre (e.g. an annual report)')`)
- **medium** · category order vs explicit rule: The 'first in table order' tie-break puts the register values first, while CX-16 says a register entry quoted in a news article is `third_party`. A trade-press page reproducing a register entry fits both CX-10 (it 'is one entry in' a list) and CX-16, and the order rule points to the register. The question text (pilot.py:197) adds 'not what it quotes', which mitigates this but sits outside the frozen CX rows. (`codebook-extension-proposal.md:28, :39`)
- **medium** · missing category / boundary: No value fits several common page kinds cleanly: a government-hosted PDF of a vendor or consultant report; a page of a state-owned enterprise or public university (institutions the master includes); a joint statement by a government body and a vendor; an official Wayback copy (extract contract §4.6 `archive`, output_contract.md:216). Each forces a choice between `formal_record`, `informal_official`, `third_party` and `unknown` without a rule. (`codebook-extension-proposal.md:37-39`)
- **medium** · supporting-text linkage: Genre is a whole-document judgement with no natural verbatim anchor. Under R-040/R-041 every non-`unknown` value needs a quote. If the extractor cannot find a quote that 'supports' `informal_official`, the code is downgraded to `unknown`, and P-5 (b) then drops the page from the transparency denominator. Downgrades would fall unevenly by page kind (a press release header is quotable; a policy PDF's genre often is not), which biases the index composition. (`SPEC.md:97-98 (R-040, R-041); INDEX-DECISIONS.md:33 (P-5 new fields = b: unknown form excluded from the denominator)`)
- **low** · reliability evidence: Agent read 39/1/0 on 40 pages in both pilots, but the 40 pages are one model's read of 6,000-character excerpts and only 4 were rare-form pages (PILOT-REPORT.md:15); register values had 1 case. 39 of 285 pilot-2 answers were below the 0.8 threshold and would be downgraded under R-081 (SPEC.md:133). (`PILOT-REPORT.md:33, :61; Agent-computed from `pilot/answers-v2.jsonl.gz` (pilot 2, n = 285 finding pages, jev-1.13.0), not a reported pilot statistic: share of answers with jev confidence < 0.8: disclosure_form 39/285`)
- **low** · redundancy: `third_party` duplicates the publisher dimension of `source_type` (§4.6). In v2.7 `source_type` has no coder (see X21), so the QC cross-check in CX §2 has nothing to check against unless X21 is resolved. (`codebook-extension-proposal.md:45; report-v2.json third_party_vs_source_type (5 + 8 off-diagonal of 285)`)

**Notes**

**Frozen (CX-01.2, signed 2026-10-25; SPEC R-025, SPEC.md:78).** Any alternative below other than `keep` requires PI re-signature of the CX row, a re-pilot or at least the R-084 fixture test for the changed wording, and (for any enum change) two contract-version steps (C-007, SPEC.md:221). T-011 must stay byte-identical to the signed text unless re-signed (PLAN.md T-011).

options.label: Keep CX-10..CX-18 as signed
options.mechanism: One jev Choice in pass 1, first chunk's value (R-044), with the pilot-2 question text.
options.benefits: No re-signature; the most reliable CX field on the pilot read; matches the signed index design.
options.risks: `mandated_report` over-captures statutory annual reports; genre codes may be downgraded for lack of a quote; boundary pages unresolved.
options.commits_to: R-025 byte-identical text; needs the X14 downgrade rule to say which supporting text counts for a genre code.

options.label: Agent-drafted: require an AI-related obligation for mandated_report
options.mechanism: Re-word CX-12/13: `mandated_report` only when the obligation concerns reporting on AI, algorithms or digital systems, named on the page; genre inference allowed only for documents whose title names AI/algorithmic reporting. Otherwise statutory annual reports code `formal_record`.
options.benefits: Restores the 'systematic AI disclosure' construct; removes a CX-03 exception; gives the extractor a quotable anchor (the named rule).
options.risks: Lower `mandated_report` counts (already ~1%); re-opens D-B (b), a signed PI ruling.
options.commits_to: Re-signature of CX-12/13 (D-B); fixture pages for the new boundary (R-084); no enum change, so no version steps beyond the v2.7 already planned.

options.label: Agent-drafted: split publisher from genre
options.mechanism: Two jev Choices: `publisher_kind` (this institution / other government body / non-government / unknown) and `document_genre` (register entry / mandated report / formal record / informal communication / unknown). `disclosure_form` becomes a deterministic cross of the two; `third_party` = publisher non-government.
options.benefits: Each question is simpler; removes the order tie-break; `publisher_kind` can replace the publisher half of `source_type` (X21) and supports the `other_body` boundary.
options.risks: Two questions where one was piloted; the derived value may differ from the signed one on edge cases; new enums.
options.commits_to: Re-signature and a re-pilot of both questions; enum additions (two version steps, C-007); index decision 7 re-read against the new values.

options.label: Agent-drafted: quote rule for genre codes
options.mechanism: Keep the wording; state in the X14 downgrade rule that genre codes are supported by the page's title or heading line (deterministic `source_title` plus the first heading), not by an extractor quote, and are exempt from R-041 downgrade if a title exists.
options.benefits: Avoids systematic `unknown` from missing quotes; no change to frozen wording.
options.risks: A title is weak evidence for genre; exempts one field class from G-002 'verbatim support'.
options.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-041 (PI approval, not CX re-signature); fixture check in T-024.

items.body:
**Current text (verbatim)**

Question to jev: *Does this page document an evaluation of this GenAI activity?* One value. If several fit, take the first in table order.

- `results_reported`: The page states that this activity was tested, evaluated, audited or monitored **and** reports a result (a metric, a finding or a conclusion).
- `conducted_no_results`: The page states that an evaluation, test, audit, pilot review or monitoring took place or is in place, but reports no result.
- `required_or_planned`: The page states that an evaluation is required (by a rule) or planned, with no evidence that it has happened. A policy finding that requires evaluation of GenAI tools takes this value.
- CX-32b: A requirement to carry out a risk or impact assessment is **not** `required_or_planned`; it belongs to `has_risk_assessment` alone (consistent with CX-37).
- CX-32c: A clause requiring periodic review of the GenAI policy itself counts as `required_or_planned`. This includes any policy with a GenAI section (e.g. a general IT policy).
- CX-32d: A required pre-use review that mixes fitness-for-purpose with security or compliance checks counts as `required_or_planned`. A pure risk or impact assessment requirement stays under CX-32b.
- `unclear`: The page makes an evaluative statement, but its subject, or whether it concerns this GenAI activity, cannot be settled. An evaluation clearly of a different tool or activity is `not_documented`, not `unclear`.
- `not_documented`: The page has no evaluation statement about this activity.
- CX-35..CX-39: no negative value; outcome claims need a described evaluation; risk/impact assessment counts only with testing or measured performance; vendor claims need a named institutional or independent evaluator; a pilot stage alone is `not_documented`.

**Reviewer findings**

- **high** · threshold interaction: Under R-081 (SPEC.md:133) 72% of the positive evaluation codes in pilot 2 would be downgraded, so the field would publish about 10 positives in 285 finding pages. The 47 low-confidence `not_documented` answers would go to 'unclear/unknown': `unknown` is not a value of this field and `unclear` has a specific signed meaning (CX-33, an evaluative statement whose subject is unsettled), so R-081 either needs a new value or overloads `unclear`. (`Agent-computed from `pilot/answers-v2.jsonl.gz` (pilot 2, n = 285 finding pages, jev-1.13.0), not a reported pilot statistic: share of answers with jev confidence < 0.8: 26 of the 36 positive codes (results_reported 9/12, required_or_planned 10/17, conducted_no_results 7/7) and 47 of 249 not_documented`)
- **high** · construct validity: CX-32c counts a clause requiring periodic review of the GenAI policy document (including a general IT policy with a GenAI section) as `required_or_planned` evaluation. Reviewing a policy text is not evaluating an AI system's performance; this makes most GenAI policies score on the governance 'evaluation' component, which then co-moves with `activity_type = policy_guidance` (itself an interim governance component, P-3 (c), INDEX-DECISIONS.md:13). (`codebook-extension-proposal.md:70 (CX-32c); PILOT-REPORT.md:64 (idx 23 'reviewed annually')`)
- **high** · state definition vs v2.7 pass 2: The frozen instrument conditions on four finding fields. In v2.7, `activity_type` and `adoption_stage` are themselves pass-2 jev codes for the same activity and `activity_name`/`tool_name` are extractor free text. Either evaluation_documented runs in a second pass-2 round after those codes (cost, latency, error propagation), or the state differs from the signed one (span marker only), which means the question is byte-identical but the instrument is not. (`codebook-extension-proposal.md:21 (CX-02: state = page text plus activity_name, activity_type, adoption_stage, tool_name); Stage5-Rulings.md:31 (DEC-010 a: jev sees page with span marked); SPEC.md:63 (R-004)`)
- **medium** · chunk interaction: Combination takes the first value in table order found in any chunk. The activity's span (DEC-010) lies in one chunk; in the other chunks 'this activity' is undefined, so an evaluative statement about anything else on a long page yields `unclear` or worse and beats `not_documented`. This inflates positives and `unclear` on long policy PDFs. (`codebook-extension-proposal.md:184; pilot/pilot.py:236-238 (min over table order across chunks)`)
- **medium** · reliability evidence: Agent read 25/5/10 on 40 pages (10 can't-tell), with remaining vendor-trial, missed-trial and CX-32b/32d boundary errors. C2-C4 wording (CX-32c scope, CX-32d, CX-33 different-tool rule) has never been run; R-084 replaces the gold set with a fixture test only. (`PILOT-REPORT.md:61, :64-66; SPEC.md:137 (R-084)`)
- **low** · boundary overlap: Boilerplate such as 'usage will be monitored' or 'the service is monitored for quality' sits between CX-31 (in place) and CX-32 (planned) and is common in policies and terms-of-use pages. (`codebook-extension-proposal.md:67 (CX-31 'monitoring ... is in place')`)

**Notes**

**Frozen (CX-01.2, signed 2026-10-25; SPEC R-025, SPEC.md:78).** Any alternative below other than `keep` requires PI re-signature of the CX row, a re-pilot or at least the R-084 fixture test for the changed wording, and (for any enum change) two contract-version steps (C-007, SPEC.md:221). T-011 must stay byte-identical to the signed text unless re-signed (PLAN.md T-011).

- **high** · scale of downgrade on CX fields: Applied to the CX fields as piloted, the threshold turns several items into mostly-unknown fields. **Current text (verbatim)**

Chunked pages (> 32k tokens, C-004): the CX-01.2 §11.1 combination rule applies to every field. Page fields take the first chunk's value; yes/no items are yes if any chunk says yes; ordered vocabularies take the first value in table order found in any chunk. **Reviewer findings**

- **high** · page verdict and completeness swept in: Read literally, R-044 makes the page verdict and page completeness 'page fields' that take the first chunk's value. A long council-minutes PDF whose GenAI item is in chunk 3 would get `no_genai`; a page whose 'see full report' link is in chunk 2 would be 'complete'. §11.1 itself limited first-chunk to the two CX page fields. The verdict needs its own rule (e.g. an order over the 8 values), which belongs to the page-verdict reviewer but is triggered by this wording. (`SPEC.md:100 ('applies to every field'), :61 (R-002: verdict and completeness are page-level codes); codebook-extension-proposal.md:184 (§11.1 names only disclosure_form and disclosure_scope as first-chunk fields)`)
- **medium** · ambiguous class membership: `content_*` are both 'page fields' (CX-01) and 'yes/no items'; R-044 lists the two rules without precedence. §11.1 resolves it (any-yes), R-044 does not. (`SPEC.md:100; codebook-extension-proposal.md:20`)
- **medium** · pass-2 span outside chunk: Pass-2 codes on chunked pages: the activity span lies in one chunk; the other chunks contain no marked activity. Running pass 2 on all chunks with an order rule inflates evaluation codes (X03); running it only on the span's chunk loses evidence elsewhere on the page. (`Stage5-Rulings.md:31 (DEC-010 a)`)
- **low** · confidence of combined code: The pilot kept the first yes chunk's confidence. With R-081, taking the first, max or min confidence changes outcomes; not specified. (`pilot/pilot.py:229-238 (combined answer = the first yes chunk's answer object)`)

**Current text (verbatim)**

R-031: When a page is not complete, the LLM extracts the follow-up links and they are sent back to the scrape phase; fetched pages then pass through the same classification. R-032: ... up to 3 hops ... A per-institution cap on followed URLs also applies ... R-033: Any link the page cites is eligible, including news and vendor pages. R-034: Each URL is fetched at most once per institution per run; every followed link records the page it came from (provenance chain). R-036: Pages fetched live during the back-fill are new source records tagged with their provenance ... They count as evidence but sit outside the original searched sample and never add to its denominator.

**Reviewer findings**

- **high** · comparability across versions: In ordinary v2.7 runs, followed pages enlarge each institution's page set (up to 3 hops), which raises the chance of a `yes` relative to v2.5 runs. R-036's 'outside the searched sample' rule applies only to the back-fill. Prevalence across v2.5 and v2.7 rows (both visible on the site, R-051) is then not comparable without a per-source `discovery_path` (searched vs followed). (`SPEC.md:91 (R-036 covers back-fill only), :119-121`)
- **medium** · attribution risk: Followed links from a village or ward page often lead to the district or county; R-033 allows any link. This feeds the error mode the unclear pilot found most often, unless followed pages are coded with `other_body` correctly. (`PILOT-REPORT.md:98 (main pilot-4 error: parent or neighbouring body's activity credited to a smaller unit)`)
- **medium** · extractor makes a selection decision: Choosing which of a page's links are 'follow-up' links is a relevance classification done by the extractor. That sits uneasily with R-001 (codes by jev only). (`SPEC.md:86; Stage5-Rulings.md:24 (DEC-003 b)`)
- **low** · stored links: See X17: hrefs are not persisted, so the extractor sees only URLs printed in text. (`render.py:65-82`)

options.label: Agent-drafted: tag discovery path on every source

options.benefits: Keeps comparability; no coding change.
options.risks: One more column.
